properties.description:
A project can optimise one of its own modules against a target it wrote down FIRST — so the work has a condition under which it is finished, and leaves a measurement a later session can re-run.

THE 21st SERVED SKILL, and the first about improving something rather than describing it. Anthony, 2026-08-21: "reflow2 is a tool for other projects... should we introduce an /optimize skill that any project could do on its modules?"

WHAT IT ACTUALLY CARRIES IS THE ORDER AND THE REFUSALS, not technique. Techniques belong to the project's own stack and reflow2 cannot supply them. It supplies: measure before forming an opinion and be willing to conclude NOTHING HERE; measure the product surface before the developer surface; find the cause by falsifiable experiment on a COPY; write the budget down BEFORE the code, derived rather than picked; re-measure against the BUDGET rather than the starting point and STOP when it is met; leave a guard asserting the STRUCTURE that makes the code fast rather than a wall-clock duration; and when a rule refuses the change, pay it in prose rather than weakening it.

THE THREE STEPS THAT EARNED THEIR PLACE each caught a real mistake in the two runs it was written from: a 14.8x speedup that was still over budget and would have shipped as a success; a duration gate that failed on suite contention and would have been fixed by raising the threshold, retiring it; and an architectural rule a cache quietly traded away, which cost one paragraph to pay honestly.

IT DOES NOT WAIT FOR CONTRACTS. The first framing put optimisation after black boxes are identified. Measured: optimising needs a WALL, a TARGET and a MEASUREMENT, and both runs succeeded with the wall ABSENT because the other two were supplied. Gating on declared interfaces would withhold the cheapest return until the most expensive one is finished.

HONEST LIMIT, WRITTEN INTO THE SKILL RATHER THAN OUT OF IT: the procedure has been run TWICE. skill_lint's OPTIMIZE_CONTRACT pins that admission alongside the nine other load-bearing clauses, so it cannot be quietly deleted once the skill feels established.
properties.name: A project can optimise a module against a budget written down first
